title: Not What These Hands Have Done
description: Not What These Hands Have Done in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Horatius Bonar wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 320.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Not what these hands have done Can save this guilt-y soul; Not what this toil-ing flesh has borne Can make my spir-it whole.

lines: Not what these hands have done
Can save this guilty soul;
Not what this toiling flesh has borne
Can make my spirit whole.
Not what I feel or do
Can give me peace with God;
Not all my prayers and sighs and tears
Can bear my awful load.
Thy work alone, O Christ,
Can ease this weight of sin;
Thy blood alone, O Lamb of God,
Can give me peace within.
Thy love to me, O God,
Not mine, O Lord, to Thee,
Can rid me of this dark unrest
And set my spirit free.
Thy grace alone, O God,
To me can pardon speak;
Thy power alone, O Son of God,
Can this sore bondage break.
I bless the Christ of God;
I rest on love divine,
And with unfaltering lip and heart
I call this Savior mine.

licence: Public domain: Horatius Bonar died in 1889.
credits: Words by Horatius Bonar (1808–1889), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
